rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track;
rows.note: Assuming "in the catalog" means every row in the Track table.

rows.sql: SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(al.AlbumId) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Album GROUP BY ArtistId))
rows.note: Assuming "most albums" means the count of rows in Album per artist, with ties included.

rows.sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC
SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS Year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assuming total revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by calendar year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS TotalSpent FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: I'll assume "total amount spent" means the sum of Invoice.Total per customer, and I'll return the top 5 by that sum.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer c JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assuming "support rep" means the Employee referenced by Customer.SupportRepId, I'll count customers per rep and return the top one(s).

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM PlaylistTrack pt JOIN Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge';
SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_purchased_tracks FROM Track t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM InvoiceLine il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId);
rows.note: Assumption: "never been purchased" means the track does not appear in any InvoiceLine.

rows.sql: SELECT BillingCountry, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue means the sum of Invoice.Total for invoices dated in 2012, grouped by BillingCountry.

rows.sql: SELECT ar.Name FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3 ORDER BY ar.Name;
rows.note: Assumption: a track's artist is reached via Track → Album → Artist, and I count distinct genres per artist.

rows.sql:
SELECT g.Name AS Genre,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine), 2) AS Percentage
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY Percentage DESC;
rows.note: I'll compute revenue per genre from invoice lines (UnitPrice × Quantity), with each genre's share of the overall total.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
  SELECT i2.CustomerId
  FROM Invoice i2
  JOIN InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
  WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
);
rows.note: Assumption: a customer "bought" a track if it appears in an InvoiceLine linked to their invoice, and genre is matched by Genre.Name.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS Month, SUM(Total) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY Month ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total for invoices dated in 2011, grouped by calendar month.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employee e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customer c WHERE c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId)

SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010 FROM (SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_date FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) WHERE first_date >= '2010-01-01' AND first_date < '2011-01-01'
rows.note: Assumption: a customer's first purchase is their earliest invoice date, and I count customers whose earliest invoice falls in 2010.

rows.sql: SELECT a.Title, ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 1) AS Minutes FROM Album a JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId GROUP BY a.AlbumId, a.Title ORDER BY SUM(t.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: total running time is the sum of Track.Milliseconds per album, converted to minutes (ms / 60000).

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS Year, SUM(Total) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY Year
),
withprev AS (
  SELECT Year, Revenue, LAG(Revenue) OVER (ORDER BY Year) AS PrevRevenue
  FROM yearly
)
SELECT Year,
       ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue,
       ROUND((Revenue - PrevRevenue) * 100.0 / PrevRevenue, 1) AS PctChange
FROM withprev
WHERE PrevRevenue IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: I'm assuming "invoice revenue" means the sum of `Invoice.Total` per calendar year, with each year compared to the prior year.

rows.sql:
WITH cust AS (
  SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spend
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_average
FROM cust
WHERE spend > (SELECT AVG(spend) FROM cust);
rows.note: I'm treating each customer's spend as the sum of their invoice totals, and the average as the mean of those per-customer totals across customers with at least one invoice.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT p.PlaylistId, p.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS artist_count
  FROM Playlist p
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
)
SELECT Name, artist_count
FROM counts
WHERE artist_count = (SELECT MAX(artist_count) FROM counts);
rows.note: I'll count distinct artists per playlist through Track → Album → Artist, and return every playlist tied for the maximum.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) AS x
rows.note: Assuming "contain tracks from more than one genre" means an invoice whose line items reference at least two distinct GenreIds.

rows.sql:
WITH rep_rev AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS RepName, SUM(i.Total) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice i
  JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
  JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
  WHERE i.InvoiceDate >= '2010-01-01' AND i.InvoiceDate < '2011-01-01'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, RepName
)
SELECT RepName, ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue
FROM rep_rev
WHERE Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM rep_rev);
rows.note: I'm assuming "invoice revenue" means the sum of `Invoice.Total` for invoices dated in 2010, attributed to each customer's `SupportRepId`.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS discontinued_products FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '1';
SELECT CompanyName FROM Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany';
SELECT c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName ORDER BY ProductCount DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS Year, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assuming "placed" means OrderDate, grouped by calendar year.

rows.sql: SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AverageFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assuming "average freight per shipper" means grouping Orders by ShipVia and joining to Shippers for the company name.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employees e WHERE e.ReportsTo = (SELECT EmployeeID FROM Employees WHERE FirstName = 'Andrew' AND LastName = 'Fuller')
rows.note: I'm assuming Andrew Fuller is the employee with FirstName 'Andrew' and LastName 'Fuller'.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2020'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, FullName
)
SELECT FullName, OrderCount
FROM counts
WHERE OrderCount = (SELECT MAX(OrderCount) FROM counts);
SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_products FROM Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM Products);
rows.note: Assuming "average product unit price" means the average of Products.UnitPrice across all products, and counting products whose UnitPrice is strictly greater than that average.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France';
rows.note: Assuming "shipped to France" means ShipCountry = 'France' in the Orders table, with every order counted regardless of ShippedDate.

rows.sql: SELECT p.ProductName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assumption: revenue per line = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), summed per product, and "top 5" means the 5 highest totals.

rows.sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE p.UnitPrice = (SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) ORDER BY c.CategoryName
rows.note: Assumption: "most expensive" means the highest UnitPrice in Products within each category, and ties are all shown.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.CustomerID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021'
  GROUP BY o.CustomerID
)
SELECT c.CompanyName, r.revenue
FROM rev r
JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = r.CustomerID
WHERE r.revenue = (SELECT MAX(revenue) FROM rev)
rows.note: I'm treating revenue as the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over order lines, grouped by customer, for orders dated in 2021.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY month HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY strftime('%m', OrderDate)))
rows.note: I'm assuming "in 2021" means OrderDate falls between 2021-01-01 and 2021-12-31, and that ties should all be returned.
The Orders table has no orders dated in 1997. Order dates run from 2012-07-10 to 2023-10-28, so the question can't be answered from this database.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_shipped_orders FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped after required date" means ShippedDate is not NULL and ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days_to_ship FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL;
rows.note: Assuming "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and the average is over the difference in days between ShippedDate and OrderDate.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel;
rows.note: Assuming "still sold" means Discontinued = '0' and "below reorder level" means UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel.

rows.sql: SELECT c.Country, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2019-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2020-01-01' GROUP BY c.Country ORDER BY OrderCount DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assumption: "customers from which country" means the Customers.Country of the ordering customer, counting orders dated in 2019, and I return only the top country(ies).

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS beverages_pct_2023 FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2023';
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), and 2023 is based on OrderDate.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12) AS t;

WITH order_values AS (
  SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS order_value
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
),
emp_avg AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, AVG(order_value) AS avg_order_value
  FROM order_values
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, ea.avg_order_value
FROM emp_avg ea
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ea.EmployeeID
WHERE ea.avg_order_value = (SELECT MAX(avg_order_value) FROM emp_avg);

SELECT s.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018' GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue means SUM(UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount)) from Order Details, filtered by OrderDate in 2018, grouped by supplier.
